title: D1-004d1 admission ledger core
description:
## Goal and why
D1-004d1 admission ledger core: add the durable Postgres admission ledger foundation — Drizzle migration/schema, admissionLedger.ts, session advisory fence, and CLI destructive-diff read — keyed by host, binding, and execution identity. Commit before effects, use advisory fencing, and fail closed on mismatch or commit failure. This is the reusable admission ledger core; it does not own consumer wiring or rollback journaling.

## Scope
One reviewable PR. ≤400 net lines. Preserve Decisions 21–24, workspace-first authority, and no pure mode. Scope is narrowed to the ledger core only: Drizzle migration/schema + admissionLedger.ts + session advisory fence + CLI destructive-diff read. D1-004d2 owns Pi first-effect admission consumers; D1-004d3 owns the WorkspaceBridge operation admission seam. D1-004e owns append-only rollback-journal creation, prepared-state reads, and recovery fencing. D1-005c is the first concrete stable-core consumer of the admission hook.

## Explicit exclusions
No rollback-journal reads or writes, publication pointer, served acknowledgement, scheduler, queue, registry/provisioner, control plane, generic policy framework, secret/raw-path output, or unrelated refactor. No Pi service decorator, createAgent.ts facade, slash/reload hook wiring, or WorkspaceBridge operation wiring (those are D1-004d2/d3).

## Acceptance and proof
Focused unit tests prove admission rows and advisory fencing commit before the first effect and reject a mismatch/commit failure without effects. Run targeted typecheck/tests and attach redacted output.

## Acceptance Criteria
See acceptance field: focused proof verifies only this bead's owned contract.

Acceptance Criteria:
Focused proof verifies: admitted binding remains non-removable after process restart and revision-directory cleanup; landing-only revisions preserve execution identity; binding-id reuse with different execution facts fails closed; concurrent admission is idempotent; kill-after-commit-before-effect leaves a deliberate permanent fence; and pre-commit/lock failure produces no effect. No rollback journal or stable-core publication behavior is implemented.

Owned stable codes: D1_ADMISSION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, D1_ADMISSION_RECORD_FAILED (must match these names exactly — do not invent variants).

Split per sizing audit 2026-07-13; siblings D1-004d2/d3 carry the consumer seams (pre-declared in PR-PLAN).

title: GH-579 Markdown recording shelf production integration
description:
## Goal
Deliver the production Markdown recording shelf approved by the GH-579 spike through three bounded phases: safe recording read APIs, protected Tiptap association, and a fully collapsible multi-recording shelf with one workspace playback owner.

## Background
Users need dictated transcript prose to feel like normal Markdown while retaining a clear association with locally retained audio. Audio and status belong in one collapsible editor-owned shelf; transcript headings, paragraphs, and lists remain ordinary editable Tiptap content. The complete list must collapse, playback must continue safely while collapsed, and microphone capture must take priority over playback.

## Locked V1 scope
- Exact-document inventory is capped at 50; no pagination or ETag.
- Audio reads return one complete bounded manifest-owned chunk; no Range support.
- Existing T11 begin/end sentinels remain the serialized format; no migration.
- Collapse state is local to the mounted editor and is not persisted.
- Association removal, inline audio nodes, word synchronization, waveform editing, and hosted STT migration are excluded.
- No backend document writer and no recording metadata on ordinary transcript prose.

## Dependency shape
T15 read API beads feed T16 Tiptap association and T17 playback. T16 and playback/polling converge in the T17 shelf. The final integration proof blocks the existing T14 ship gate.

## Definition of done
Every child bead meets its acceptance checklist, exact gates, evidence requirement, and cross-provider review. The graph has no cycles, package boundaries remain intact, guarded giant files do not gain orchestration, and final browser proof covers real multi-chunk audio at desktop and mobile widths.

## Evidence
Each child records commands, outputs, pass/fail, changed files, residual risks, and review result in bead comments. No private microphone audio, transcript content, tokens, or internal artifact paths enter committed evidence.\n\n## Frozen shared-file ownership map
- recordingApiClient inventory list/DTO decode: .14 only.
- recordingApiClient complete-chunk binary/header parser: .12 only, after .14.
- .13/.15/.17/.21 are import-only consumers and may not call status() for shelf/playback.
- RecordingManifest/manifestStore/recordingStore create/list seams: .2 only; .4 consumes the exported lookup.
- recordings.ts and shared routes.test.ts extraction: .20 only; .3/.4 own disjoint modules/tests.
- MarkdownEditor mount extraction: .18 only; atomic extension/completion cutover: .9 only; shelf uses the extracted seam.

## Review RACI
Per-bead review checks diff+acceptance only. .5 and .11 check phase seam compatibility and cite focused dispositions without re-litigation absent failing evidence. .19 checks the frozen tree, maintainability, privacy/security, and aggregate regression evidence.

## Frozen provider mount ownership
- .14 alone mounts RecordingInventoryStore in existing TranscriptionProvider and owns its provider-file edit.
- .12 runs after .14 and alone inserts PlaybackProvider as a focused child; it does not restructure/remount the provider.
- .13 runs after .12 and owns only controller coordinator injection plus ComposerDictationAdapter callback wiring.
- .21 must not edit either provider file; it owns only resolver consumer/lifecycle registration.
- .15/.17/.22/.24 are provider/client import-only consumers.

## Review commands and inputs
- Per-bead: implementation diff + bead acceptance + exact gate evidence; first-level GPT-5.5 high and independent Sol final review, fix/repeat until clean.
- Phase .5/.11: phase diffs, focused dispositions, and seam-compatibility evidence only; no product re-litigation absent a failing gate.
- Final .19: exact frozen tree, all phase dispositions, thermonuclear maintainability, privacy/security, and aggregate regression evidence.
- Plan/bead architecture: Grok + Claude Opus CLI + Gemini adversarial panel; accepted findings are fixed and rerun when provider capacity permits.
notes: Hard prerequisites before any impl:start: the candidate tree must contain BrowserRecordingController, DocumentRecordingAction/StartRecordingDialog/capsule ownership, T10 delete-audio companion behavior, TranscriptSentinel, and insertRecordingTranscriptAtCursor with their merged T08/T10/T11 proof. Review matrix: every bead gets focused diff+acceptance cross-provider review; .5 and .11 review phase seam compatibility; .19 reviews frozen-tree maintainability/privacy/aggregate regressions without design re-litigation absent new evidence. Epic close supplies T15-T17 evidence only; T14 remains the separate SHIP gate.

title: GH-579 T15a define bounded recording-read contracts
description:
## Goal
Define browser-safe shared contracts and stable errors for fixed-limit exact-document recording inventory plus complete bounded audio-chunk reads.

## Background
The shelf needs safe metadata and deterministic candidate-chunk selection without sidecar paths, capture credentials, an unbounded timeline, pagination, ETag, Range, or a second playback-plan endpoint.

## Scope
- Define GET document-recordings request/response types for one supported existing documentPath: .md, .markdown, .txt, or .text.
- Return at most 50 newest-first items plus truncated.
- Each item contains recording id; stable 1-based ordinal; lifecycle; start/end/duration; transcript version; immutable create-time rolling chunkDurationMs; chunk count; recording-level audio availability/deletion state; and safe failure code.
- Define ordinal as the rank over all retained manifests ordered (createdAt ASC, recordingId ASC); newest-first projection and truncation never renumber it.
- Define provenance: new manifests persist create-time chunkDurationMs; legacy manifests derive a read-only maximum-positive-saved-span fallback and are never rewritten. No usable timing yields a stable playback-unavailable reason, never current server policy.
- Define complete-chunk response/error metadata for recordingId plus integer index, including shared constants/parser for Content-Type, Content-Length, X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Index, X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Start-Ms, and X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-End-Ms.
- Reuse existing TRANSCRIPTION_RECORDING_AUDIO_MISSING for unavailable/missing/deleted chunk audio and existing auth/not-found/bounds errors; do not add a second audio-unavailable code and keep shared code free of node imports and Buffer. out_of_inventory is exclusively a T17 client snapshot state, never an HTTP error; retained recording-id audio reads remain valid outside the newest-50 projection.

## Non-goals
No store/route implementation, audio bytes, UI, playback, Tiptap, per-chunk array, pagination, ETag, Range, playback-plan endpoint, or document mutation.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Types encode every field/provenance/ordinal rule above and exclude secrets, paths, transcript body, hashes, and provider details.
- [ ] Fixtures cover Markdown/plain-text paths, lifecycle/audio states, legacy timing fallback, unusable timing, truncation without renumbering, and malformed input.
- [ ] Existing API compatibility is preserved.

## Gate commands
- pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-transcription typecheck
- pnpm --filter @hachej/boring-transcription test
Pass means both exit 0 with focused shared-contract tests.

## Evidence
Record exported types/errors, synthetic examples, legacy fallback/ordinal fixtures, test names, and browser-safe source proof.

## Required completion record
- [ ] Implementation stays inside the stated ownership boundary.
- [ ] Exact gates pass, or a concrete skip reason and replacement evidence is recorded.
- [ ] Evidence contains commands, relevant output, changed files, residual risks, and assignment token.
- [ ] Architecture/docs are updated for public seams, otherwise N/A is recorded.
- [ ] Focused cross-provider review passes; fix and repeat until clean before STATE impl:done.

Never record secrets, private transcript/audio content, tokens, Authorization headers, or internal artifact paths. Preserve unrelated changes, stable errors, package/workspace isolation, and giant-file guards.\n\n## Preflight fail-closed gate
Before impl:start, verify plugins/boring-transcription/src/shared/errors.ts, shared/types.ts, server/recordings/types.ts, and the merged T06/T09 recording store/worker tests exist. Stop rather than invent a parallel contract if absent.
notes: Contract correction: inventory items expose immutable rolling chunkDurationMs, chunkCount, total/end duration, and recording-level availability, but no unbounded per-chunk array. Complete-chunk responses expose safe index/start/end timing metadata. No playback-plan endpoint, pagination, ETag, or Range.

title: GH-579 T16e expose workspace-isolated marker navigation registry
description:
## Goal
Expose a narrow editor-owned association registry so T17 can navigate recording id to marker and marker activation back to a shelf row without importing private editor internals or querying the global DOM.

## Background
Multiple workspaces/editors may open identical document paths. Navigation must be provider-scoped and panel-aware, following the existing filesystem open-editor/action registry pattern.

## Scope
- Register/unregister mounted marker targets by workspace/editor identity, document path, recording id, and panel id.
- Expose typed focus/scroll-to-marker command with reduced-motion behavior.

title: GH-579 T17a implement bounded multi-chunk playback owner

## Goal

- Maintain one audio element/current Blob/object URL; revoke on transition, stop, error, unmount, path/workspace switch, or replacement playback.
- Pause previous playback before starting another; deduplicate requests and ignore stale responses.

- Return complete bytes with stored Content-Type and accurate Content-Length plus X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Index, X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-Start-Ms, and X-Boring-Recording-Chunk-End-Ms from the exact manifest entry, using only T15a shared constants/parser.
- Reject unsaved, failed, missing, deleted, oversized, or wrong-workspace audio with stable errors.

title: PR 1: native Pi session creation and rename
description:
## GitHub
#775

## Delivers
Browser-memory New chat plus direct-local first-send handoff to one native Pi session/no wrapper.

## Contract
Before Send, browser owns an ephemeral `BrowserDraft` with no durable session ID. First Send carries an in-tab idempotency key and transitions `new → native_persisted(nativeSessionId) → prompt_submitted → reply_committed | prompt_failed | unknown`. - Empty chat creates no durable session.
- First Send creates exactly one native Pi transcript and no wrapper.
- Persistence-success/response-loss retry returns one native ID; prompt failure and restart unknown states are explicit.

- Boring and pi resume show the same materialized session.

comments.text: Heartbeat: root cause found. gh-781 (stale working badge) already largely fixed on main via recent commits (session-activity SSE stream + useWorkingSessionIds reconciliation, packages/workspace/src/front/sessionActivity.ts). gh-778 (external-entrypoint session not appearing) root cause: WorkspaceAgentFront's activity-stream onActivity handler only dispatched a status CustomEvent, never checked whether the session id was known to the list, so a session created out-of-band stayed invisible until remount/manual refresh. title: SQLITE_BUSY: use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for durable-store writes
description: Follow-up from PR #1128 review (MED residual): busy_timeout=5000 does NOT cover the real contention shape. runTransaction issues a deferred BEGIN (sqlStorage.ts:49) and appendEventOnce reads (readIdempotencyKey SELECT) then writes inside it (eventStreamStore.ts:117-135). On a deferred read->write lock upgrade SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY IMMEDIATELY, ignoring busy_timeout. Concurrent appends from two runtime bindings can therefore reach publishChannelEvents' poison policy and KILL a live channel. FIX: BEGIN IMMEDIATE for write transactions. PROOF: concurrent-append test across two store instances over one file, no channel poisoned. MUST land before the flag is enabled in production.
close_reason: Delivered inside PR #1128 (5bedbed0b): SqlTransactionMode immediate on all 3 write paths; worker-thread proof, deferred mode reliably reproduces the lock error.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Claiming: BEGIN IMMEDIATE fix for eventStreamStore write transactions + concurrent-append proof test, same PR #1128, worktree .worktrees/1009-durability.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Done. SHA: 5bedbed0b on feat/1009-durable-streaming (PR #1128).

Fix: added SqlTransactionMode ('deferred'|'immediate') to runTransaction/RunTransaction in sqlStorage.ts (deferred stays default, not a blanket change — no other callers exist today but future read-only ones are unaffected). All three SqliteEventStreamStore write paths (appendEvent, appendEventOnce, appendAgentEvent) now pass 'immediate' explicitly, matching SqliteAgentRequestLedger's transactional idiom. busy_timeout=5000 (from the prior round) now actually applies, since BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquires the write lock up front instead of hitting SQLite's non-retried read->write upgrade case.

Mutation proof: packages/agent/src/server/events/__tests__/eventStreamStore.concurrentAppend.test.ts
1. Real concurrency test — two node:worker_threads workers, each with its own node:sqlite connection to ONE on-disk file, run the actual sqlStorage.ts runTransaction primitive with the exact allocateSeq/readIdempotencyKey read-then-write shape, 60 iterations each. mode='immediate': 120/120 commit, zero errors surface to either caller. mode='deferred': reliably reproduces "database is locked" (SQLITE_BUSY) on every run (verified 5x) — this is the without-the-fix failure, observed directly, proving the immediate-mode test is non-vacuous.
2. Wiring test spies on runTransaction and asserts the three real eventStreamStore.ts call sites pass 'immediate'. title: Connect-time SSRF enforcement for user-registered MCP
description: The syntactic hostname/IP-literal pre-filter in plugins/boring-mcp/src/shared/index.ts (validateUserRegisteredMcpEndpoint) is NOT an SSRF control: it never resolves DNS, so an attacker A-record (e.g. 127.0.0.1.nip.io, or DNS rebinding) bypasses it entirely, and a validated https:// endpoint can still 302-redirect to a private/metadata address. mcpSdkTransport.ts now sets requestInit.redirect='error' for user-registered sources as a stopgap, but that only blocks redirects — it does not stop a first-hop connection to an attacker-controlled DNS name that resolves to a private IP. Real connect-time SSRF enforcement requires one of: (1) resolve-then-pin — resolve the hostname to an IP before connecting, re-run the private/metadata blocklist against the resolved IP, and pin the TCP connection to that IP (so a TOCTOU re-resolution can't swap it), or (2) route all user-registered MCP traffic through an egress allowlist/proxy that enforces network-level isolation from cloud metadata services and internal ranges. This must land before any user-registered MCP source is admitted in an environment that can reach production networks or a cloud metadata service.

Connect-time resolve-then-pin makes all of these moot — do not chase them in the string filter.

title: Durable store: sync driver blocks event loop up to 5s
description: Follow-up from PR #1128 round-3 review (MED-LOW tradeoff, now the expected path): node:sqlite DatabaseSync is SYNCHRONOUS, so a busy_timeout=5000 wait BLOCKS THE NODE EVENT LOOP for up to 5s. With BEGIN IMMEDIATE, waiting is the normal outcome rather than an immediate throw — correct trade (bounded stall beats a poisoned channel + lost events), but under many concurrent runtime bindings the failure mode becomes latency/head-of-line blocking. OPTIONS: async sqlite driver, or shorter busy_timeout with bounded retry. Also cheap: rename EventStreamMeta.nextOffset (it holds the LAST seq, not the next offset — it caused a reviewer misread this session). Evaluate before enabling BORING_CHAT_DURABLE_STREAM at scale.
